scope: Every existing event dated 2026 at assignment start (198 records; through 2026-09-11)

key.title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire

records.note: NDMA's post-winter report supports at least 80 deaths, later than the inquiry report's 79. Nighttime January 17 in Karachi remains January 17 UTC. Align the prose with the numeric toll; omit unsupported shop/office victim details.

changes.description: A fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Karachi on the night of 17 January 2026. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority subsequently reported at least 80 deaths and dozens of injuries; an earlier inquiry report counted 79 deaths. The fire spread through the multistorey commercial building.

key.title: West Bandung landslide

records.note: 02:30 WIB January 24 is 19:30 UTC January 23. The February 1 figure was 74 body bags, not necessarily 74 identified individuals. Police confirmed 80 identified victims on February 10; do not equate body bags with people or call this a final toll.

changes.description: Heavy rain triggered a landslide in Pasirlangu village, West Bandung Regency, at about 02:30 local time on 24 January 2026 (23 January UTC), burying homes. By 10 February, West Java police had identified 80 victims. Identification of additional remains was continuing.

key.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse

records.note: The roughly 400 figure is a provisional civil-society estimate, not a confirmed count of miners alone; AP reported at least 200. March 3 is supported by Reuters (published March 4), but that separate collapse has a disputed toll and should not be folded into January's deaths. Exact January onset time unavailable. The numeric field still reflects a provisional estimate; a confirmed comparable toll and January UTC onset remain unresolved.

changes.description: Heavy rain caused a landslide and mine collapses at the Rubaya coltan mining complex in North Kivu on 28 January 2026. Rebel-appointed authorities reported at least 200 deaths. A civil-society representative subsequently estimated roughly 400 deaths; that higher figure remained provisional and was not limited to miners.

key.title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks

records.note: January 29 is the military operation's beginning, not the coordinated BLA assault (January 31). The reported components are 216 militants, 36 civilians and 22 security personnel = 274, not 225; all are military-reported, not independently confirmed. The original identity key is retained for audit only. The proposed scope is a multi-day campaign, not a proven single-day BLA attack. Its start date must not be presented as the date of all 274 deaths; assault versus military-operation allocation remains unresolved.

changes.title: Balochistan attacks and military operations
changes.description: Pakistan's military reported 216 militants, 36 civilians and 22 security personnel killed during a campaign in Balochistan from 29 January to 5 February 2026. The operation began two days before coordinated Baloch Liberation Army attacks on 31 January. The combined reported toll of 274 includes militants killed in military operations as well as victims of the attacks.

key.title: Kwara State attacks

records.note: Core attack and minimum 162 are supported; contemporaneous attribution differs (Lakurawa versus Boko Haram). Specific Sadiku attribution, >200 final toll, mosque summons, named victim occupations and 38 abducted are not all established by the checked reporting. Narrow to supported facts; evening local onset remains February 3 UTC.

changes.description: Armed extremists attacked Woro and Nuku in Kaiama, Kwara State, on the evening of 3 February 2026. Local officials and the Red Cross reported at least 162 deaths, while the state government initially gave a lower count. Homes were burned and residents abducted. Reports differed over the attackers' affiliation, and no group immediately claimed responsibility.

key.title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing

records.note: Dawn's later update gives 36. Reuters calls the attack the capital's deadliest in more than a decade, contradicting 'nearly a decade'. Friday prayer time is safely February 6 UTC. Dawn-derived content below is limited to the updated toll.

changes.description: An attacker opened fire at the gates of the Khadija Tul Kubra Shia mosque in Islamabad's Tarlai area during Friday prayers on 6 February 2026 before detonating explosives. The death toll subsequently rose to 36. More than 100 people were injured. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

key.title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting

records.note: Core date, victims and total supported. Kinship qualifier and historical rankings omitted because checked sources differ or do not establish them.

changes.description: An 18-year-old former student killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge on 10 February 2026: her mother and 11-year-old brother at a home, and five students and a teacher at the secondary school. The perpetrator also died by suicide, bringing the total dead to nine. Twenty-seven people were reported injured.

key.title: Abiemnom massacre

sources.name: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

records.note: Core date and attributed toll supported. Omit disputed injury count and unestablished duration/attacker count.

changes.description: Armed attackers raided Abiemnom in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area on 1 March 2026. Local authorities reported 169 deaths, including 90 civilians. The UN mission said about 1,000 people sought shelter at its base. Accounts differed over the attackers' affiliation and the number injured.
sources: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

key.title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides

records.note: 125 deaths supported; sources date the sequence March 9-10, March 10, or early March 11. Exact UTC onset and road/farmland damage remain unresolved.

key.title: Jilli market airstrike

records.note: April 11 event, April 12 publication. 100 is a rights-group toll, not official final count. Military defended the operation; exact UTC onset unavailable. A single verified UTC onset and reconciliation of the competing casualty accounts remain unavailable; the attributed minimum is not a confirmed final total.

changes.description: A Nigerian airstrike hit Jilli market near the Borno-Yobe border on 11 April 2026. Amnesty International reported at least 100 civilians killed, citing survivors and medical contacts. Other estimates were higher. The military said it had targeted militants; accounts of the strike and the casualty total remained disputed.

key.title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion

records.note: May 22 evening (same UTC date), place, 82 deaths, investigation and decadal comparison supported. Earlier 90 revised downward; missing are separate.

key.title: Mindanao earthquake

records.note: 07:37 local June 8 = 23:37 UTC June 7. Date-only correction; final 107 deaths, injuries/missing, housing totals, PHP 71bn loss and uplift claims remain unverified.

key.title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes

records.note: 6125 is official as of August 3, reported August 4. Detailed destruction and USD 37bn estimate not corroborated; ABC says nearly 200 collapsed buildings, not 800.

changes.description: Two earthquakes, reported at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, causing widespread destruction, particularly in La Guaira. Official figures cited by UNICEF recorded 6,125 deaths as of 3 August. Homes and infrastructure were damaged and many residents displaced.

key.title: Gansu flash flood at Weiyuan scenic area

records.note: July 26 afternoon is same UTC date. Initial ten deaths rose to 25; 23 injured and investigation supported.

key.title: Kumamoto earthquake

records.note: 16:27 JST = 07:27 UTC July 28. August 3 data: 38 dead, 98 injured, 8383 evacuees. Other damage counts not established. AP puts explosion before mall collapse.

changes.description: An earthquake measured at magnitude 7.1 by Japan's Meteorological Agency struck Kumamoto at 16:27 local time on 28 July 2026. Prefectural figures as of 3 August recorded 38 deaths, 98 injuries and 8,383 evacuees. Damage included an explosion and collapse at Aeon Mall in Kashima and a chimney collapse at a paper mill in Yatsushiro.

key.title: Militant drone-and-ambush attack on police checkpoint in Hangu

records.note: July 29 and 11 police dead supported; attackers killed differ (AP 15, ARY eight). Drone detail, prior assault comparison and precise UTC onset not established.

key.title: US–Saudi airstrikes kill 20 Iran-backed militiamen in Iraq as US strikes on Iran resume

records.note: PMF reported 20 members killed. IRGC advisers may be additional. Overnight July 28-29 requires UTC check; resumed Iran strikes and causal link to Kuwait not fully established.

key.title: Wildfires in southern Greece kill three firefighters

records.note: Core date, locations and three deaths supported. Broader evacuation, damage and containment claims omitted.

changes.description: Three firefighters died during wildfire response operations in southern Greece on 29 July 2026. Two died in a fire in the Rethymno region of Crete. A third was found unconscious near a fire in the Gytheio area and pronounced dead in hospital; authorities had not established the cause of his death.

key.title: Firefighting helicopter crash in San Juan kills seven

records.note: 10:26 local = 13:26 UTC July 29; seven deaths supported. Training preceded flight to La Rioja. Occupant occupations and ranking not established.

changes.description: A Bell 412 helicopter contracted by Argentina's Federal Emergency Agency crashed near Ischigualasto Provincial Park in San Juan on 29 July 2026, killing all seven occupants. It had previously taken part in training and was travelling toward La Rioja to assist firefighting operations. Contact was lost at about 10:26 local time.

key.title: Russia launches massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine

records.note: 70 missiles/280 drones supported; Reuters nine deaths, EFE earlier eight, versus record ten. Family and Kryvyi Rih totals may overlap. Polish incursion and UTC onset not confirmed.

key.title: Avalanche on Broad Peak leaves climbers missing, four confirmed dead

records.note: All ten confirmed dead August 1. Bodies located/recovered are not final casualty count. Around 09:00 local July 30 remains same UTC date.

changes.title: Broad Peak avalanche kills ten climbers
changes.description: An avalanche struck ten climbers on Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram range on the morning of 30 July 2026. All ten, including Nirmal Purja, were subsequently confirmed dead. Recovery operations continued after the first bodies were located, with weather and terrain hindering access.

key.title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan

records.note: AP reports 34 dead, 32 recovered and two to retrieve. July 30 occurrence versus July 31 publication distinguished. Exact time unavailable but no evidence of UTC crossover. Absence of evidence of a crossover does not establish the UTC date; withhold pending an onset time or sufficiently specific time-of-day account.

key.title: IRGC claims retaliatory strike on US base in Kuwait amid Iran war

records.note: Fatality belongs to July 30 company-building strike, not July 31 base claim; exact clock time unavailable. The proposed July 30 is the reported local occurrence date; UTC conversion remains unverified.

changes.title: Iranian strike on Chinese company building in Kuwait kills worker
changes.description: Kuwait's Defence Ministry said an Iranian attack hit a building belonging to a Chinese company in northern Kuwait on 30 July 2026, killing one worker and causing substantial damage.

key.title: Flash floods and landslides in Dien Bien Province

records.note: Matched event is 2025. Around 04:30 August 1 ICT = July 31 UTC. Ten deaths/seven injuries in later VTV report. Check 2025 collision before moving.

changes.description: Flash floods and landslides struck Dien Bien Province early on 1 August 2025 local time (31 July UTC), after heavy rain. A subsequent provincial tally reported ten deaths and seven injuries. Homes and roads were damaged and several communities isolated.

key.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv

records.note: Nine dead and 33 injured supported for overnight July 31-August 1. Exact onset for UTC conversion not established. Appears duplicate of 'Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten' dated August 1; reconcile and retain only one incident.

key.title: Terrorist attack on labourers in Kulgam

records.note: Evening July 31 remains same UTC date. Second injured worker later died; update toll rather than adding separate event.

changes.description: Gunmen shot two workers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kelam, Kulgam district, on the evening of 31 July 2026. One died initially and the second later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to two.

key.title: Calabar flood and landslide crisis

records.note: Ten is a month-long total published August 1, not deaths on July 31. Primary report supports flooding/landslides but no dated ten-person tally. A defensible onset anchor and overlap with individual incidents remain unresolved.

key.title: Apartment building fire kills four in Changsha

records.note: Fire service statement reproduced by Xinhua gives 03:54 August 1 local = 19:54 July 31 UTC; six rescued, four died by August 2, two receiving treatment. All material claims match. Only one retrieved publication/source chain; a second independent link is still needed before canonical source replacement. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

key.title: Bombing at Moscow restaurant kills three

records.note: Three was initial total; August 3 embassy statement cited by AP gives five dead and 19 injured. Earlier toll included woman carrying bomb. Evening Moscow remains August 1 UTC.

changes.title: Bombing at Moscow restaurant kills five
changes.description: A bomb exploded near the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in Moscow on the evening of 1 August 2026. Authorities initially reported three deaths, including the woman carrying the device, a security guard and a visitor. A subsequent Russian embassy statement reported five dead and 19 injured.

key.title: Plane crash near Nazca kills 13

records.note: August 1 crash, 13 occupants and tourist nationalities corroborated. Exact six-kilometre location and aircraft timing/UTC not independently established; avoid full verification.

key.title: Shooting at In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls

records.note: City and local public radio update injuries to seven. 14:30 MDT is 20:30 UTC August 1. Retrieved accounts vary over whether three deaths include gunman; retain reported three without claiming three homicide victims. Resolve victim/perpetrator breakdown separately. Publication is withheld until the victim/perpetrator scope of the total is reconciled.

changes.description: A shooting near an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls on the afternoon of 1 August 2026 left three people dead and seven injured, according to the city's public update. Police said the immediate threat had ended and the investigation was continuing.

key.title: Israeli strikes kill at least seven in Gaza

records.note: Seven since dawn supported by AFP; distinguish from separate rolling ministry totals. Omit warehouse count and clinic damage not established.

changes.description: Gaza's civil defence reported seven people killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip since dawn on 1 August 2026. An Israeli strike also destroyed medical supplies stored for Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to hospital and Palestinian health officials.

key.title: Seven armed robbers killed in Kabul police operation

records.note: Robber identity and exchange-of-fire account are police allegations, contested by former justice minister. 21:00 Kabul remains August 1 UTC. Sixteen arrests may be a separate operation; do not conflate without evidence.

changes.title: Taliban police report killing seven alleged robbers in Kabul
changes.description: Taliban police said seven men accused of armed robbery were killed during an operation in Kabul's Police District 8 on 1 August 2026. Police described a confrontation at about 21:00 local time. A former Afghan justice minister subsequently described the killings as extrajudicial; the police account was not independently established.

key.title: Assam flood death toll reaches 82

records.note: 82 was announced late Friday July 31, reported Saturday August 1. It is season-to-date, not daily deaths. Current affected population was about 193000; 1.1m may refer to another snapshot. District death breakdown not corroborated. The proposed July 31 is a reporting snapshot, not a verified onset. Its Assam component overlaps the India-wide monsoon tally; publication requires a defensible non-overlapping episode boundary.

changes.description: Assam's disaster authority reported a cumulative monsoon-flood death toll of 82 by late 31 July 2026. Reports published the next morning said roughly 193,000 people in five districts remained affected. This is a season-to-date toll, not deaths on one day.

key.title: Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten

records.note: Likely duplicate of July 31 'Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv'. Sources report nine, not ten, in the overnight July 31-August 1 attack; ten may be borrowed from July 30 nationwide strikes. Merge after establishing onset; do not sum both records.

key.title: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza

records.note: Core Sunday attacks and minimum 18 supported. Unsupported Saraya breakdown omitted. August 3 aggregate must be reconciled, not added.

changes.description: Israeli airstrikes across Gaza on 2 August 2026 killed at least 18 Palestinians, including children, according to medics. Strikes hit Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis. The toll may overlap the 18 newly killed people in the health ministry's next-day 24-hour bulletin and must not be counted again.

key.title: Firefighting helicopters collide in Greece killing two

records.note: Date, collision, two fatalities, nationalities and survivors supported. Daytime firefighting on August 2 remains that UTC date.

key.title: Suicide bombing at anti-militant rally kills 14 in Swat

records.note: August 2 Kabal rally attack supported. Totals differ: 14, 15 and later secondary 17; police/civilian breakdown and injured counts vary. Do not combine incompatible snapshots. Exact onset unavailable.

key.title: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia kill eight

records.note: DW supports eight nationwide but lists Udmurtia and Belgorod, and depicts Wildberries in Samara, not Moscow. AP's next-day account reports nine. Location composition, 635 interceptions, Belgorod four and UTC coverage require reconciliation.

key.title: Russian glide bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia

records.note: AP supports the detailed account; Reuters confirms date and toll. Sunday evening event, Monday publication; no UTC rollover.

key.title: Sudanese army drone strike on Darfur court kills 35

records.note: Later victim documentation gives 46 deaths and seven injured, but labels findings preliminary. Time differs (AP afternoon; DVS 10:30 local), both August 2 UTC. Use attributed latest count, not unsupported dozens injured/missing.

changes.title: Drone strike on Darfur community court kills at least 46, rights group reports
changes.description: A drone strike hit Zawiya Ghara community court in North Darfur during a court session on 2 August 2026. Emergency Lawyers initially reported at least 35 deaths. Darfur Victims Support Organization later reported 46 civilian deaths and seven injuries in preliminary documentation based on interviews with families and witnesses. Rights groups attributed the strike to the Sudanese army.

key.title: Israeli strike kills two in Gaza City

records.note: Specific vehicle strike, two deaths, Sheikh Ajlin and Monday evening supported. Evening August 3 local is same UTC date. Keep separate from earlier ministry 24-hour bulletin only after checking reporting cutoff.

key.title: Israeli fire kills 19 Palestinians in Gaza

records.note: Ministry's August 3 release supports 18 newly killed plus one previous-wound death, not 19 deaths necessarily occurring August 3. Likely overlaps August 2 entry's 18. Cannot count both totals independently; exact rolling-window cutoff and unique victims unresolved.

key.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Gelendzhik beach kills seven

records.note: Early Interfax/Meduza accounts gave seven deaths. Ust-Labinsk Info's August 4 updated lead reports eight, including four children, and Novaya Gazeta Europe's September 2 incident table also records eight for August 3. The local article retains superseded lower figures in its body; do not treat those as a final tally. The headquarters post independently supports 58 injured but does not state eight deaths. The attack occurred around 09:00-10:00 local August 3, the same UTC date. Russia attributes the drone to Ukraine; whether air defences caused its fall remains unresolved and is not asserted as fact.

changes.title: Drone crash on Gelendzhik-area beach kills eight
changes.description: A drone crashed onto a beach at Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik on the morning of 3 August 2026. Later reporting put the toll at eight deaths, including four children, with 58 injured. Russia attributed the drone to Ukraine; whether air defences caused it to crash remained uncertain.

key.title: Landslide kills 14 at Ethiopian monastery

records.note: AP's full report supports date, monastery, region, rain, 14 deaths, seven injuries and people unaccounted for. 07:00 local = 04:00 UTC August 3. One retrieved source chain; obtain second independent URL before replacing canonical sources. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

key.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills five

records.note: Governor's five dead/six injured and Novoselki/Chekhov supported. Overnight onset not precise enough to establish August 3 versus 4 UTC; sources share governor statement rather than independent casualty confirmation.

key.title: Russian guided bombs kill three in Sumy

records.note: 02:08-02:17 EEST August 4 = 23:08-23:17 UTC August 3. Checked accounts give older victim's age 75, not 76; injury toll later expanded, so omit static four.

changes.description: Russian guided aerial bombs struck Sumy between 02:08 and 02:17 local time on 4 August 2026 (3 August UTC). The attack killed two girls aged five and ten and a 75-year-old woman, according to Ukrainian reports, and injured other residents. Homes and civilian infrastructure were damaged.

key.title: Serviceman kills four in shooting near Sevastopol

records.note: Four dead (one soldier/three civilians), four injured and detention supported. AP explicitly says governor did not specify when it happened: August 4 is report date, not proven occurrence date. Victim ages not established.

key.title: CRPF officer shooting in Assam kills four

records.note: Two colleagues and perpetrator dead, one injured supported; August 12 follow-up still describes three. No support located for injured colleague's later death. Morning August 4 may require exact clock for UTC boundary. Any rewrite must use 'died by suicide' without method.

key.title: Russian drone strike on Mykolaiv kills elderly woman

records.note: Victim age, seven injured including two children, and two destroyed homes supported. Night of August 3-4 not precise enough for UTC day; do not use publication date as onset.

key.title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza

records.note: August 4 is bulletin date; two newly reported deaths may include the August 3 vehicle strike. Cumulative 73377 corroborated, but exact death dates/unique victims and full injury/rubble claims not established.

key.title: Lightning strike kills footballer in Thailand

records.note: Afternoon August 4 remains same UTC date. Tournament was Golok FA Cup, not a league match; transliteration Sofwan/Safwan varies. Reports give nine or more injured, not a verified upper bound of twelve.

changes.description: A lightning strike during a Golok FA Cup match at Santiphap Stadium in Sungai Golok, Narathiwat, on the afternoon of 4 August 2026 killed 24-year-old Yala FC player Sofwan Awae. At least nine others were reported injured.

key.title: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv kill two

records.note: Core attack/missile counts supported; sources give 17 combined and later two city deaths, not record 21 with 3+18. Title/number mismatch. Onset after midnight August 5 local implies potentially August 4 UTC; precise onset and final combined toll unresolved.

key.title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza

records.note: All quoted ministry totals supported as an August 5 reporting snapshot, but rolling 24h fatalities cannot all be dated August 5. Unique victims and overlap with incident-level entries not established.

key.title: Israeli airstrike on south Lebanon kills one

records.note: One death/location/date supported; latest ministry tally 12 injured supersedes initial 11. Rome round had concluded, not simply under way. Daytime strike safely August 5 UTC.

changes.description: An Israeli drone strike hit the roof of a prayer hall at a cemetery in Tebnine, Bint Jbeil district, on 5 August 2026. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported one person killed and twelve injured, updating an initial report of eleven injuries. The strike came as a round of Lebanese-Israeli talks in Rome concluded.

key.title: Sri Lanka floods and mudslides kill seven

records.note: Disaster began before August 5; eight already reported August 4, later nine by August 25. Eight/seven title mismatch. Geographic and time windows differ; exact onset/toll scope and 11000 evacuated unresolved. Do not treat cumulative impacts as August 5 deaths.

key.title: India monsoon floods and landslides kill more than 100 since July

records.note: AFP supports 133 since early July, including 87 in Assam. August 5 is release date, not event date. Assam portion overlaps the 82-death Assam record. Must choose non-overlapping disaster scopes and establish onset; do not add both full tolls.

key.title: Russian strike on grain ship in Odesa region kills one

records.note: Mera Queen, flag, wheat, one killed/three injured supported. Odesa report dates strike evening August 5; trade publication uses August 6. Preserve conflict rather than treating report date as proof. Exact UTC date requires primary confirmation.

key.title: Hezbollah blast kills two Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon

records.note: 55th is reserve paratroopers, not armored brigade. Explosive's age/nature under investigation, so title should not imply freshly planted Hezbollah attack as settled. August 5 occurrence versus August 6 announcement distinguished.

changes.title: Explosion in southern Lebanon kills two Israeli soldiers
changes.description: Two Israeli reservists from Battalion 2855 of the 55th Reserve Paratroopers Brigade were killed and four seriously wounded in an explosion during an operation in Majdal Zoun on 5 August 2026, the Israeli military announced the following day. The circumstances of the explosive device were under investigation.

key.title: Mass shooting in Caswell County, North Carolina kills three

records.note: Local full report establishes before 8am August 5 (same UTC day), home/area, three deaths including suspect, hospitalized relative and investigation. Toll includes perpetrator.

key.title: Mudslide buries household in Zhashui County, Shaanxi

records.note: Xinhua's August 6 dispatch quotes the county flood-control headquarters: the household was buried August 5, with one confirmed dead and two missing. It also supports the July 30-August 5 maximum rainfall figure. Missing people are not included in lives_lost. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

key.title: Russian drone attacks across Ukraine kill six

records.note: Reuters supports six deaths, three each in Balakliia and Sumy region, but says overnight without times to determine August 5 versus 6 UTC. Sumy city's guided-bomb attack injured 12, not 13; not all attacks are established as drones. Compare the separate Lozova entry to avoid combining separate attacks.

changes.title: Russian strikes kill six in Balakliia and Sumy region
changes.description: Ukrainian authorities reported three people killed in overnight strikes on homes in Balakliia and three in attacks in Sumy region. Reuters reported at least 19 wounded in Sumy-region settlements, another 12 in Sumy city, and six in a drone attack on a van in Kherson region.

key.title: Israeli airstrike on Beit Lahia kills one

records.note: August 6 is the bulletin date, not a proven death or attack date. The report says one person died of earlier wounds during a rolling 24-hour period; it does not identify Beit Lahia or a new airstrike. Cumulative 73,382 and five wounded are supported. Exact death time and incident linkage remain unresolved.

changes.title: Gaza hospitals report one death from earlier wounds
changes.description: An August 6 medical bulletin reported one Palestinian who died of earlier wounds and five injured people received by Gaza hospitals during the preceding 24 hours. It reported a cumulative death toll of 73,382 since October 2023.

key.title: Storm deaths in the Philippines reach at least 27

records.note: The record is a nationwide cumulative storm series, not a discrete Northern Luzon event on August 6. Official reporting begins July 30; the August 20 OCD figure rose to 29 reported deaths, while later reports add other storms and cannot be substituted without matching scope. Reported versus validated counts also differ. Includes potential overlap with August 9 Baguio and Batangas records; do not add all three totals. Resolve episode boundary and validated toll before replacement.

key.title: Rain-triggered house collapse kills six in Pratapgarh, India

records.note: Contemporaneous reports place the collapse around 02:00 IST August 6, which is August 5 UTC. Six deaths are supported; the existing family-member enumeration incorrectly sums to seven. Replace it with the supported total. ThePrint full-page access was denied; its indexed PTI report and NDTV corroborate the core facts.

changes.description: A house collapsed during heavy rain in Mahuli, Pratapgarh district, at about 2 a.m. local time on August 6, killing six members of a family, including two young children.

key.title: ATF agents kill two men during Nashville firearms operation

records.note: TBI confirms Thursday afternoon August 6, the two identities and ages, and an exchange of gunfire during an ATF operation. One victim was a minor, so 'two men' is inaccurate. TBI says the sequence remains under investigation; the unsupported gun-pointing sequence is removed, not adjudicated.

changes.title: ATF operation in Nashville ends with man and teenager fatally shot
changes.description: James Salinas, 32, and Denzel Molina, 16, were fatally shot during an ATF firearms operation on Landers Avenue in Nashville on August 6. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said agents encountered two people and gunfire was exchanged; it was investigating the circumstances. No officers were injured.

key.title: Russian drone strike on Lozova train station kills two

records.note: The August 6 police report and railway workers' August 7 identification explicitly date the attack August 6. Both men, ages 52 and 59, and 11 injured are supported. The later publication date was mistaken for the incident date.

changes.description: Russian drones struck railway infrastructure and the station in Lozova on August 6, killing two railway workers aged 52 and 59 and injuring 11 people, according to regional police.

key.title: Thailand school shooting kills nine

records.note: The morning August 7 school attack and August 8 rise to nine are supported. Nine includes two grandparents killed at home and the shooter, not nine school victims. Sources differ on the shooter's age; omit it. A single pupil's later death is supported, so avoid plural students killed.

changes.description: A student killed his grandparents before attacking Debsirin Nonthaburi School on the morning of August 7, killing five staff members and injuring more than 20 people. The shooter also died. A wounded pupil died on August 8, bringing the reported total, including the shooter and the grandparents, to nine.

key.title: Firefighting helicopter crash near Utah wildfire kills two

records.note: The incident record identifies a CH-54A and loss of contact at 10:41 a.m. August 7. Both occupants were pilots. The foundation locates the crash near Kanosh, not Richfield itself; use the more precise location. Cause remains under investigation.

changes.description: Two pilots died when a contracted CH-54A firefighting helicopter crashed near Kanosh at about 10:41 a.m. local time on August 7 while dropping water on the Widemouth 2 Fire.

key.title: Wildfire kills bulldozer operator in Oregon

records.note: The foundation's employer-derived memorial explicitly dates the death August 6, matching AP's Thursday account; FireRescue1 says August 7. Prefer the memorial and AP, while retaining this contradiction. FireRescue1 places the missing-dozer alert at 16:30 local, before UTC midnight. Age and fire entrapment are supported.

changes.description: Jason Ensign, a 47-year-old equipment operator, died while operating a bulldozer at the Wrights Spring Fire in Oregon on August 6. Rapid fire growth cut off his escape route while he helped construct fire lines.

key.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Kyiv region kills three, including child

records.note: Three deaths are supported for Brovary, while the wider Kyiv/capital-region total later became four. Do not substitute the wider toll into this narrower record. Later police reporting has four injured, not three. The overnight attack needs a time to distinguish August 7 from 8 UTC.

changes.title: Russian drone strike kills three in Brovary district
changes.description: A Russian drone strike destroyed a family home in Brovary district, killing a three-year-old child and his grandparents. Three other family members and a neighbor were hospitalized.

key.title: IS-linked militants kill at least 13 in eastern Congo village attack

records.note: Both sources support at least 13 killed and attribution to ADF/IS-linked militants. AP reports Saturday, whereas the local report explicitly says Friday August 7 around 19:00 local (17:00 UTC). This is not merely a publication-date difference that can be silently resolved. Omit the imprecise Uganda-border characterization.

changes.description: An attack attributed to ADF militants killed at least 13 civilians in Banana Ecole, Mambasa territory, Ituri. Local reporting described homes and vehicles burned and villagers abducted. Reports disagree whether the attack occurred August 7 or 8.

key.title: Helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro kills four

records.note: Firefighters were called around 11:10 local August 8. Four occupants, wooded Tijuca National Park location near Vista Chinesa, and Robinson R44 registration/model are supported. This is August 8 UTC.

key.title: Explosive drone attack on police substation kills officer in northern Colombia

records.note: Local follow-up dates the attack to the night of August 7; without an hour, August 7 versus 8 UTC remains unresolved. One officer killed and another wounded are supported. Remove unrelated tollgate and presidential-term detail rather than treating those as evidence of this incident's date.

changes.description: Explosives dropped from drones struck the San Roque police substation in Curumani, Cesar, killing one officer and wounding another. Local reporting places the attack on the night of August 7.

key.title: Russian missile strike on Kharkiv apartment block kills two

records.note: Police and regional administration reports support the August 9 morning missile strike, Saltivskyi residential location, two men aged 50 and 66 killed, and more than a dozen injured. The injury count increased from 21 to 23; existing nonspecific wording accommodates that update.

key.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill five in Russia's Belgorod region

records.note: The death toll rose from three to five and then six. Interfax's August 9 evening report attributes the sixth death to recovery of another man's body from the damaged apartment building, citing the regional operational headquarters. This is an update to the same overnight August 8-9 attack, not an additional incident. Exact fatal-strike timing remains insufficient to select August 8 versus 9 UTC; publication remains withheld.

changes.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod kills six
changes.description: Russian authorities reported six people killed in a drone attack on Belgorod during the night of 8-9 August 2026. The toll increased after another body was recovered from an apartment building. Russia attributed the attack to Ukraine.

key.title: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza

records.note: The August 9 WAFA bulletin reports two deaths received in 24 hours, including one from earlier wounds, not three new strike deaths on that date. It supports cumulative 73,386. The cited same-day gunfire report describes three injuries, not deaths. Incident-specific support for three killed, nine wounded, and the asserted target locations was not established; do not infer those from cumulative totals.

key.title: Habagat floods and landslides kill three in Batangas, Philippines

records.note: ABS-CBN supports a provincial total of three reported August 9, but its accessible page lacks the narrative needed to date each death. Manila Bulletin places Latumbo's death Saturday night August 8, not August 9. Full three-death chronology remains unresolved. These deaths potentially overlap the nationwide Luis/Maymay/monsoon cumulative record. The provincial/nationwide casualty overlap remains unresolved.

key.title: Houthi strikes on Mokha kill at least seven in Yemen

records.note: August 9 attack is supported, but later accounts conflict: Reuters quotes the military's seven deaths/30 injured; Anadolu has seven/35; AFP via South24 reports eleven (three civilians, eight military)/32. The record's seven/15 is preliminary and may omit later attack waves. Establish whether the intended scope is the first strike or all Sunday attacks before selecting a replacement toll.

key.title: Two tribal elders shot dead in South Waziristan, Pakistan

records.note: The date, identities, tribal affiliation, two deaths and unknown attackers are supported. The detailed police account locates the shooting near Darozanda while traveling toward Zarmilan; clarify rather than imply the destination was the precise site.

changes.description: Unidentified gunmen killed tribal elders Haji Gul and Malik Badshah while they traveled toward Zarmilan in Lower South Waziristan on August 9. Police said the attack occurred near Darozanda in Toi Khulla tehsil; both men belonged to the Suleman Khel tribe.

key.title: Sofa factory fire in Riyadh kills 16 Bangladeshi workers

records.note: Bangladesh ministry/embassy reporting supports 16 Bangladeshi deaths at the sofa factory, ten from Naogaon and others from Natore/Rajshahi. Fire reported around 14:00 local August 9, also August 9 UTC. The total is the reported Bangladeshi toll, not an independently established count of all nationalities.

key.title: Landslide on rain-soaked hillside in Baguio kills 10

records.note: All 13 reported victims were accounted for by early August 11: ten dead, three survivors. The record combines this final toll with an earlier missing-person count. Sources vary on exact evening hour but agree August 9, also UTC. These ten overlap the nationwide monsoon cumulative record; do not count twice.

changes.description: A landslide struck houses in Guisad Surong, Baguio, on the evening of August 9 during prolonged monsoon rain. By early August 11, rescuers had accounted for all 13 reported victims: ten died and three survived.

key.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk kills 13

records.note: Later AP reporting gives 13 killed and 78 injured, superseding 39 injured. Remove the ranking and unsupported child detail from the replacement. Russian officials reported casualties; Ukraine said it targeted a refinery, so do not independently assert intentional civilian targeting. Other retrieved reporting describes the night leading into August 10. No sufficiently precise fatal-strike time was established to distinguish August 9 from 10 UTC; withhold despite the supported toll update.

changes.description: A Ukrainian drone attack struck Nizhnekamsk on the morning of August 10. Russian authorities reported 13 deaths and 78 injuries. Ukraine said it targeted an oil refinery in the city.

key.title: Russian artillery strike on Buhaivka village in Kharkiv region kills five

records.note: Reports citing regional prosecutors support the August 10 morning artillery attack on Buhaivka's residential area, five killed and houses destroyed. The source dates the attack itself, not merely a casualty bulletin.

key.title: Palestinian girl dies of wounds from Israeli fire in Gaza

records.note: The named 13-year-old's August 10 death is supported. Retrieved WAFA syndications say she was wounded several days earlier, not exactly two, and do not establish the head-wound detail. This death can overlap a subsequent Gaza rolling bulletin; do not add it without reconciliation.

changes.description: Thirteen-year-old Saba Naim Abdullah al-Hashash died on August 10 from wounds sustained when Israeli forces shot her several days earlier in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, according to WAFA.

key.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake in western Colombia kills at least 331

records.note: Magnitude 7.4 and August 10 07:34 local/12:34 UTC are supported. PAHO's indexed September 4 report relays UNGRD's September 3 tally of 331 dead and 466,606 affected. Missing persons remain separate; early 111/132 and later 312/321 totals were interim. PAHO page returned 403 but indexed report is accessible.

changes.description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia at 12:34 UTC on August 10, with its epicenter near San Jose del Palmar, Choco. UNGRD's September 3 assessment reported 331 deaths and 466,606 people affected. Buildings collapsed and landslides damaged communities in the affected region.

key.title: Ukrainian drone hits Donetsk gas station, killing truck driver

records.note: The report supports the August 10 claim, 45-year-old truck driver killed and station employee wounded, but derives entirely from the Russian-installed official. No independent confirmation was located. Describe it as his allegation rather than presenting responsibility as independently established. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

changes.title: Russian-installed official reports fatal drone strike on Donetsk fuel station
changes.description: Denis Pushilin, the Russian-installed head of occupied Donetsk, said a Ukrainian drone struck a fuel station in the city's Proletarsky district on August 10, killing a 45-year-old truck driver and wounding an employee.

key.title: Two custodians killed in shooting at Chicago elementary school

records.note: Later medical-examiner reporting establishes murder-suicide, superseding the initial uncertainty. Police place the shooting at 15:40 local August 10, also August 10 UTC. Both were transported to hospital where they died, not necessarily found dead at school. The two-death total includes the perpetrator.

changes.title: Murder-suicide at Chicago elementary school leaves two custodians dead
changes.description: A shooting at Mark Twain Elementary School in Chicago's Garfield Ridge neighborhood on August 10 killed custodian Amalia Bautista Perez, 48, and her 63-year-old coworker. The medical examiner classified their deaths as homicide and suicide respectively. No children were in the school.

key.title: Russian combined strike on Zaporizhzhia kills seven

records.note: Reported explosions around 00:30 EEST August 11 are 21:30 UTC August 10. The plant's August 27 statement updates the earlier attack to eight employees killed and 26 injured. Its separate August 27 strike caused no casualties. Replace preliminary figures and omit ancillary missile-origin/mourning-day claims rather than leave unchecked details.

changes.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhstal kills eight workers
changes.description: A Russian ballistic-missile attack struck the Zaporizhstal steel plant around 00:30 local time on August 11, or August 10 UTC. The plant later reported eight employees killed and 26 injured in that attack, which halted production.

key.title: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region kill five

records.note: Primary police report lists four killed across August 10-11, one aged 15, and eight wounded including three children. Prosecutor reporting places the boy's death on the evening of August 10 and two other minors among injured, not dead. AP initially reported three deaths. The record's five dead/three minors is not established, and the aggregate's UTC period is unresolved.

key.title: Russian strike on tanker truck in Odesa region kills two

records.note: The August 11 afternoon report establishes two killed and three wounded in the tanker-truck attack. Replace ancillary later-apartment detail with the directly sourced incident; the truck contained oil residue. The toll remains attributed to the regional administration.

changes.description: A Russian strike hit a tanker truck containing oil residue in Odesa region on August 11. Regional administration head Oleh Kiper reported two people killed and three wounded.

key.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh region kills one

records.note: Reuters supports one death, two injuries and warehouse fires according to the governor. It describes an overnight attack without enough timing to choose August 10 versus 11 UTC. The victim's precise age/district and national 396-drone total were not established from retrieved evidence; use a narrower description once the date is resolved.

changes.description: Voronezh governor Alexander Gusev reported one person killed and two injured in an overnight drone attack, with falling debris setting warehouse facilities on fire. His statement was reported August 11.

key.title: Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihama in Bab el-Mandeb kills six

records.note: August 11 attack and Yemeni coastguard's six reported deaths/ten injuries are corroborated, including two rescuers. However, August 14 Indonesian foreign-ministry reporting still classifies its crewman as missing, whereas earlier reports count him dead. Do not silently resolve that discrepancy or label all six confirmed. A later reconciliation is needed for the confirmed-death total. Ship flag also varies between reports, so omit it.

changes.description: Yemen's coastguard reported six people killed, including two rescuers, and ten injured in successive missile strikes on the cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on August 11. Later Indonesian reporting still listed one crewman among the missing, leaving a discrepancy with the initial nationality breakdown.

key.title: Man kills wife and four children in Winfield, Kansas murder-suicide

records.note: Police identify six dead and an 08:50 local 911 call on August 11, also that UTC date. Retrieved reporting establishes the family deaths but not marriage/parentage for every child; omit those ancillary assertions and the imprecise 'early' qualifier. Total includes the suspected perpetrator. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

changes.description: Police found Ronald H. Williams Sr., 53, Kelly George, 44, and four children aged three to nine dead in a Winfield home on August 11. Williams had called 911 around 8:50 a.m. saying he had killed his family and intended to kill himself. Police investigated the deaths as a murder-suicide.

key.title: Flash floods in Adré kill three

records.note: The local August 12 report explicitly dates the rain and flooding to the afternoon of August 11 and supports the town/department/province. Witness accounts describe five swept away, three dead and two rescued; do not treat all five as deaths. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

key.title: Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba killing 46

records.note: The numeric field's 46 matches the later police toll; the description's 44 is stale. Passenger/missing counts remain uncertain and are not interchangeable with confirmed deaths. Replace the ancillary disaster-declaration detail with a concise incident summary supported by the reports.

changes.description: An overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba on August 11 after encountering strong waves. Police reported 46 deaths by August 13, while the disaster-management agency said 77 people had been rescued. Authorities had not established a definitive passenger or missing-person count.

key.title: Russian drone strikes on Kherson kill two

records.note: The overnight attack killed two, including a woman inside her home, and injured two in Tsentralnyi district. Available reporting does not give the strike time needed to choose August 11 or 12 UTC. A separately reported August 12 afternoon fatal strike must not be silently merged.

key.title: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia region kill one

records.note: The 1,000-plus strikes and one death refer to August 11, reported August 12, with nine wounded. The Epicentr attack is a separate overnight event. The record conflates a daily casualty aggregate with the shopping-center strike; the fatal incident time/identity must be resolved before assigning a single UTC date.

changes.description: Regional authorities reported one person killed and nine injured during Russian strikes across Zaporizhzhia region on August 11. A separate overnight attack damaged the Epicentr shopping center in Zaporizhzhia.

key.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Novorossiysk kills three

records.note: Three deaths/24 injuries apply to Krasnodar region, not solely Novorossiysk; the child is specifically linked to the city. Overnight timing leaves August 11/12 UTC unresolved. The supported scope correction below avoids attributing all regional casualties to the port.

changes.title: Ukrainian attacks on Krasnodar region kill three
changes.description: Governor Veniamin Kondratyev reported three deaths, including an eight-year-old child, and 24 injuries in overnight attacks across Krasnodar region. Novorossiysk's port infrastructure and grain terminals were also damaged.

key.title: Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod region kill two civilians

records.note: TASS establishes a past-24-hour bulletin on August 12 with two killed and three wounded, not two deaths necessarily occurring August 12 UTC. The record itself juxtaposes a later three-death report without establishing whether it updates the same incidents. Resolve individual victims and reporting interval before choosing a toll/date.

key.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea kills civilian

records.note: Both reports relay Aksyonov's claim of one civilian death in Novosyolovskoye during the night leading into August 12. Without an incident time, the UTC date could be August 11 or 12. Attribution is a Russian-installed official's claim, not independent verification.

key.title: Landslide on Mumbai chawl kills seven

records.note: 03:48 IST August 12 is August 11 UTC. Later PTI reporting gives eight dead and search termination, superseding seven and 'more feared trapped'. Early injury count four increased to seven. Use a concise summary without retaining stale missing-person language.

changes.title: Landslide on Mumbai chawl kills eight
changes.description: A rain-triggered landslide struck homes at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar, Mumbai, around 3:48 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. The death toll rose to eight before search operations ended on August 13; seven others were injured.

key.title: Israeli fire kills one in Gaza

records.note: Anadolu explicitly corrects its initial report of one death: the person was critically wounded, with two injured in Beit Lahia and four in separate incidents. The recorded death therefore lacks support; do not republish a retracted preliminary fatality. A ministry cumulative total cannot establish that this particular strike killed someone. Subsequent victim outcome remains unestablished.

key.title: Military Apache helicopter crash near Salado kills two

records.note: Army/local reporting supports August 12 afternoon near Salado, two pilots killed in an AH-64 Apache from Fort Hood and a resulting grass fire/evacuations. The follow-up confirms both occupants died and the cause remained under investigation. Local afternoon is the same UTC date.

key.title: Severe storms and tornadoes kill three in US Midwest

records.note: Reports published August 12 describe Tuesday August 11 storms. Three associated deaths are reported, but the Portage house-explosion cause was still being investigated and the Ohio death was an indirect emergency-access death. Exact UTC times of the geographically separate deaths were not established. Do not present all three as direct tornado deaths or use publication date as occurrence date.

changes.description: Three deaths were reported amid the August 11 Midwest storms: a child struck by a falling tree in Indiana, a person killed in a Portage house explosion whose cause was under investigation, and an Ohio resident whom emergency responders could not reach because of flooding.

key.title: Landslide in Rolpa district kills ten

records.note: August 12 evening at Kotalbara is supported. Initial ten dead/three missing contradicts the record's two missing. Police reported 12 recovered dead and one child missing August 15; August 19 reporting says 13 killed without explaining whether the last missing child was recovered or presumed dead. Confirm that distinction before updating lives_lost. The separate August 13 Sunchhahari landslide is not this event.

key.title: Ferry fire off Bali kills one

records.note: Ministry received notice at 04:20 WITA August 12 and AP places onset about 04:15, both August 11 UTC. One death and 211 rescued are supported by later reporting. Passenger manifests were inconsistent; omit the provisional five missing rather than imply a final accounting.

changes.description: The Putri Yasmin ferry caught fire between Bali and Lombok around 4:15 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. Rescuers evacuated 211 people and recovered a 19-year-old Indonesian woman's body, authorities reported.

key.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia kills five

records.note: The matching five-dead/20-injured report is dated August 11, with its update at 02:10 local, and describes the August 10-11 attack. This strongly duplicates the original August 11 'Russian combined strike on Zaporizhzhia kills seven' row, whose toll later reached eight and UTC date is August 10. No separate August 13 five-death event was established. Withhold this duplicate candidate pending identity reconciliation; do not publish both.

key.title: Russian drone strike on passenger train in Odesa region kills two

records.note: The August 13 train strike, Berezivka district, two crew deaths and 340 passengers evacuated are supported. Remove the unestablished jet-powered subtype and evacuation destination from the replacement.

changes.description: A Russian drone struck a passenger train in Berezivka district, Odesa region, on August 13, killing the driver and his assistant. Authorities evacuated the 340 passengers, including 67 children; no passengers were reported injured.

key.title: Armed man fatally shot by police at Auckland shopping centre

records.note: Police's own statement supports the air-rifle theft report around 14:00, pursuit, confrontation under the shopping-center overpass and death despite first aid. August 13 afternoon NZST is August 13 UTC. Circumstances remain investigated; verification here is of the attributed account, not a finding that lethal force was justified.

key.title: Explosion at Port of Rotterdam kills one

records.note: Police and local reporting support one dead, several injured, about 11:30 CEST August 13 at the port's Europoort/Gunvor facility, and an investigation rather than an established cause. This is 09:30 UTC the same date.

key.title: Multi-vehicle crash near Accra kills at least 11

records.note: Local reporting citing the fire service supports August 13 around 04:00 in Ghana (UTC), Ofankor Barrier on the Accra-Kumasi highway, eleven killed and thirteen injured. Earlier five-death headline text is superseded by the updated article.

key.title: Explosion during ordnance disposal in Sevastopol kills five

records.note: EMERCOM confirms four personnel deaths and Reuters adds the security guard, quoting the governor's disposal-after-drone-attack account. EMERCOM says the night of August 13 without an exact time, so August 12 versus 13 UTC remains unresolved. Crimea should be identified as occupied Ukrainian territory.

key.title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians in Gaza

records.note: Two August 13 deaths are supported. The 'first fatalities in more than a week' qualifier cannot describe all Gaza deaths, given earlier ground-fire and wounds deaths; omit it. Israel described Abu Kamil as a Hamas commander while Gaza authorities identified his police role; retain both attributed characterizations.

changes.description: Israeli strikes killed Gaza police official Jamal Abu Kamil in Gaza City and Hudhaifa Kawara in Khan Younis on August 13, according to Palestinian medical and interior-ministry sources. Israel said Abu Kamil was a Hamas commander.

key.title: Landslide and water seepage in Chamoli tunnel kills seven workers

records.note: THDC's statement puts the water/debris ingress at about 18:20 IST August 13, same UTC date. Seven confirmed deaths are supported, with additional workers missing, not included in that toll. Injury counts vary (12/13/14), and the physical cause remains investigated; omit the precise injury number and avoid presenting seepage/landslide causation as finally established.

changes.description: A sudden influx of water and debris entered the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project's unfinished tunnel in Chamoli around 6:20 p.m. local time on August 13. At least seven workers died and others were injured, with searches continuing for missing workers.

key.title: Record rainfall floods eastern Japan, killing nine

records.note: JMA identifies the episode as August 13-14; initial Thursday flooding supports the August 13 start. The governor's August 27 briefing gives thirteen dead and one missing, over 4,500 homes damaged. Do not include the missing person as dead or treat nine as the final toll. Replacement uses the later official count.

changes.title: Record rainfall in Chiba kills thirteen
changes.description: Record rainfall on August 13-14 flooded communities in Chiba Prefecture. The governor reported thirteen deaths, one person missing and damage to more than 4,500 homes by August 27.

key.title: Explosion at Fujian shipyard kills firefighter

records.note: Official chronology: fire 13:09, crews arrived 13:25, explosion 14:10, firefighter died 18:50, all August 13 local/UTC. Twelve initially injured includes the firefighter who later died, leaving eleven surviving injured. Retrieved primary-derived accounts do not establish the personal name/age; omit them.

changes.description: A fire at Huahai Shipyard in Gantang, Fu'an, began at 13:09 local time on August 13. An explosion at 14:10 injured ten firefighters and two other people; one firefighter died in hospital that evening. Authorities were investigating the cause.

key.title: Fire at Greater Noida wood-cutting shop kills one worker

records.note: PTI dates the fire to the intervening night of August 13-14, not a precise time. One died; the other was later stable, not necessarily still critical. An exact time is needed for UTC. Full ThePrint open was denied; indexed PTI text supports the incident and rescue.

changes.description: A fire at a wood-cutting shop in Shahberi, Greater Noida West, left Altamas dead and Aman injured. Police said both were rescued unconscious and taken to hospital after the overnight fire on August 13-14.

key.title: Car crash into truck in Nagpur kills two students

records.note: NDTV's August 13 article explicitly says early Wednesday morning, August 12, and local August 12 reporting corroborates that day. UTC could be August 11 or 12 without the crash time. Two dead and one injured are supported. The teenagers were taking a drive while awaiting a birthday celebration, not necessarily traveling to the party.

changes.description: Two 17-year-old students died and a third teenager was seriously injured when their car hit a stationary truck in Nagpur early on August 12 local time. Police said they had gone for a drive while waiting for a friend's birthday celebration.

key.title: Bomb blast kills defected naval officer in Sevastopol

records.note: Initial official statements did not name the officer; later registry-based reporting and the August 16 follow-up support Shageyev's identity and August 13 death. Russian authorities' allegation about Ukrainian direction is not independently established. Use attributed wording and identify Crimea as occupied Ukrainian territory.

changes.description: An explosion in Sevastopol on the morning of August 13 killed a Russian naval officer later identified in reporting as Robert Shageyev, a former Ukrainian submarine commander who defected in 2014. Russian authorities said they detained a woman and alleged Ukrainian intelligence involvement; that allegation was not independently verified.

key.title: Suspected murder-suicide shooting on Staten Island kills two

records.note: NYPD-derived reporting places the shooting around 11:10 local August 13, same UTC date. The woman died at the scene, but the man was transported and died later in hospital, contradicting 'both declared dead' at the residence. Two total deaths include the suspected perpetrator.

changes.description: Police responded to a shooting at a Garth Court home on Staten Island around 11:10 a.m. on August 13. Dana Foley, 39, died at the scene, while Dakota Suckstorff, 27, died after being taken to hospital. Police investigated a suspected murder-suicide.

key.title: Firecracker factory explosion near Sivakasi kills two workers

records.note: The later Thursday report supports two deaths after the second injured man died in hospital. It supports testing a chemical-mixing machine, but an inquiry into cause is not a determination of safety failures. Initial one-death PTI report is superseded.

changes.description: Two men died after an explosion while testing a new chemical-mixing machine at a fireworks factory near Sivakasi on August 13. One died at the site and the second in hospital. Police opened an investigation into the cause.

key.title: Russian double drone strike on Sumy region kills woman and nine-year-old boy

records.note: Regional-administration reporting supports the morning August 14 attack by two jet-powered UAVs, Buryn community, the mother's and child's ages, two killed and four injured, including father and grandmother with severe burns. The home, fire and damage details are corroborated.

key.title: Russian glide bomb hits apartment block in Donetsk region, killing one

records.note: The attack is in Kramatorsk and one death is supported. Injury reports increased from 16/17 to 22. Overnight timing leaves August 13 versus 14 UTC unresolved. Omit the precise floors-destroyed count rather than retain an unchecked structural detail.

changes.description: A Russian guided-bomb attack damaged an apartment building in Kramatorsk, killing one person and injuring others. Reports published August 14 described an overnight strike, with the reported injury count later rising to 22.

key.title: Helicopter crash in Sehmatal, Saxony kills pilot

records.note: The police statement marks 09:55 August 14 as the time police learned of the crash, not a measured crash time. Pilot death, workers' rescue attempt, fire, forestry operation and investigation are supported. Replace the exact crash-time assertion and omit the unconfirmed lime-spreading detail.

changes.description: A helicopter crashed and caught fire during forestry work near Neudorf in Sehmatal on the morning of August 14. Workers pulled the 29-year-old pilot from the aircraft, but he died at the scene. Police received the report at 9:55 a.m. and opened an investigation with the aviation accident authority.

key.title: Series of shootings in Michigan kills six including gunman

records.note: Six total deaths including Hickman, one injured and three locations are corroborated, with officers responding before noon August 14. Retrieved reports establish that the suspect was found dead but not the medical conclusion of suicide; remove that unverified method assertion.

changes.description: Five people were killed in shootings in Missaukee County on August 14, and suspect Chad Hickman, 39, was later found dead. Police found victims at two homes and in woods near Whitlock Lake; another person was critically injured. The six-death total includes the suspect.

key.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Indonesia kills at least 54

records.note: The existing UTC date is correct: 05:58 WITA August 15 equals 21:58 UTC August 14. BNPB reported 68 identified dead by August 17, superseding 54; this is the whole affected region, not just Nagekeo. Small tsunami waves are officially reported, but omit the unestablished 'Level II' terminology.

changes.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Flores kills at least 68
changes.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Flores at 21:58 UTC on August 14, or 5:58 a.m. local time on August 15. BNPB reported 68 identified deaths by August 17. The earthquake damaged buildings, triggered landslides and small tsunami waves, and displaced residents.

key.title: Coal mine explosion in Cucunuba kills six miners

records.note: ANM confirms all six trapped workers died in a methane-associated explosion at Porvenir 1. Morning August 14 is supported. ANM describes an indefinite suspension ordered after the accident; retrieved primary evidence does not establish the record's no-permit/prior-suspension assertions, so remove them.

changes.description: Six miners died in a methane-associated explosion at the Porvenir 1 coal mine in Cucunuba on August 14. Colombia's National Mining Agency confirmed the deaths and ordered operations suspended pending compliance with safety requirements.

key.title: Toxic gas leak at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard kills nine workers

records.note: Incident about 09:00 local August 14 is the same UTC date. A worker died August 19, raising the toll to ten. Government reporting supports hydrogen sulfide exposure. Injury and missing counts varied in early coverage, so omit an unsupported final tally.

changes.title: Toxic gas at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard kills ten workers
changes.description: Workers at Ferdous Steel's Sitakunda shipbreaking yard were exposed to toxic gas inside a vessel on August 14. Authorities identified hydrogen sulfide. The reported death toll rose to ten after another worker died in hospital on August 19.

key.title: RSF attack on Um Arada near El Obeid kills at least 18 civilians

records.note: Friday August 14 attack, location and displacement are corroborated. Europa Press gives at least 18 people killed and 17 injured from local sources; rights/local accounts document more than fourteen civilian deaths. These are differing reporting thresholds, not proof all eighteen were civilians. Preserve attribution and omit the unsupported exact distance/family total.

changes.title: RSF attack on Um Arada reportedly kills at least eighteen
changes.description: An RSF attack on Um Arada southwest of El Obeid on August 14 killed at least eighteen people and wounded seventeen, according to local-source reporting carried by Europa Press. Rights and local reports documented more than fourteen civilian deaths and displacement toward El Obeid.

key.title: Mudslide in Changxing, Zhejiang kills one and leaves three missing

records.note: The county report specifies 06:30 CST August 14, or 22:30 UTC August 13. One dead/three missing is explicitly a preliminary 14:30-local count; no later confirmed outcome was located. Do not convert missing people into fatalities. Remove unrelated regional warning detail.

changes.description: A rain-triggered mudslide collapsed a house in Tanlongqiao village, Heping town, Changxing, around 6:30 a.m. local time on August 14, or August 13 UTC. County authorities reported one confirmed death and three people missing that afternoon.

key.title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby

records.note: The three-month-old boy's death and eleven injured, including two children, are supported. The official account says nighttime; no strike time was located to distinguish August 14 and 15 UTC.

key.title: Flash flood and landslide in Ponferrada area kill two women

records.note: Emergency calls at 19:38 CEST August 15 support the same UTC date. Two women died; the missing elderly man was found unharmed, so 'fate of others unknown' is stale. RTVE later reports four injured, including two children. The narrower replacement avoids disputed river/precise refuge characterization.

changes.description: A flash flood and debris flow struck Manzanedo de Valdueza and nearby settlements in the Ponferrada area on August 15, killing two women. Four other people, including two children, were injured. An elderly man initially missing was found unharmed.

key.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children

records.note: The ministry's eleven deaths (seven Ansar, four Deir Zahrani) and nineteen wounded are supported. Accounts describe overnight/dawn strikes without enough precise timing for both sites to assign one UTC date. Strip ancillary flight, building-height and condemnation details, but retain the date blocker.

changes.description: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported eleven deaths in Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir Zahrani during the night leading into August 15 local time: seven in Ansar, including three children, and four in Deir Zahrani. Nineteen people were reported wounded.

key.title: Russian night attack on Kryvyi Rih kills one and injures six

records.note: Later regional reporting updates one dead/six injured to two dead/fourteen injured. The 04:25 time is a casualty update, not necessarily the strike time. August 15 versus 16 UTC remains unresolved for the overnight attack.

changes.title: Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih kills two
changes.description: An overnight Russian missile and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih damaged industrial facilities. Regional authorities later reported two people killed and fourteen injured after another body was recovered on the morning of August 16.

key.title: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in Khan Younis

records.note: WAFA explicitly distinguishes shooting Saturday evening August 15 from body recovery Sunday August 16. Evening local is August 15 UTC. The stated ceasefire-year context is unnecessary and unestablished; remove it.

changes.description: Fourteen-year-old Suhail Masoud Shalouf was shot by Israeli forces on al-Tina Street south of Khan Younis on the evening of August 15, according to WAFA. The Palestinian Red Crescent recovered his body the following day.

key.title: Historic flooding in Indiana kills seven

records.note: Seven is a cumulative storm/flood-related toll reported August 16, not seven deaths necessarily occurring that day. NWS places the rainfall/flood episode earlier in the week. This overlaps the August 12 Midwest three-death record, which already includes Indiana victims. Resolve incident boundaries, direct/indirect deaths and duplicate victims before publication.

key.title: Shooting at Lexington, Kentucky park kills one and injures four

records.note: Police responded shortly before 19:00 EDT Saturday August 15, before 23:00 UTC. August 16 was reporting/update date. One victim died and four were injured, including children. Later police reporting documents an arrest; omit initial suspect uncertainty.

changes.description: A shooting during the East End Day gathering at Charles Young Park in Lexington on August 15 killed sixteen-year-old Di'Zhon Robertson and wounded four people, including children. Police responded shortly before 7 p.m. local time.

key.title: Ukraine launches one of its largest aerial attacks of the war on Russia, killing at least six

records.note: The six reported deaths and Russian claims of hundreds of drones are supported, but this is an overnight multi-region aggregate without UTC incident times. Do not infer occurrence date from the August 16 release or independently validate the claimed interception count/ranking. Resolve the fatal incidents before publishing a single-date total.

changes.title: Ukrainian attacks across Russia reportedly kill six
changes.description: Russian authorities reported at least six deaths after widespread overnight Ukrainian drone attacks reported August 16. Attacks affected the Moscow region and other areas, including industrial and energy facilities.

key.title: Wildfires on Greek island of Salamina kill two and injure nine

records.note: Two deaths and Sunday midday August 16 fires in Peristeria/Selinia are supported. Later reporting identifies an elderly couple; initial unknown-identity wording is stale. Injury counts differ between accounts, so remove the unsupported nine rather than retain it.

changes.title: Wildfires on Salamina kill two
changes.description: An elderly couple died during wildfires on Salamina on August 16. Fires broke out around midday in Peristeria and Selinia, prompting evacuations, including hundreds of people taken off the island by sea.

key.title: Polish tourist bus overturns on Hungarian motorway killing 12

records.note: 01:00 CEST August 16 is 23:00 UTC August 15. Later DW reports 47 injured, 10 seriously; the original at-least-10 figure was an early minimum.

changes.description: A bus carrying 57 Polish passengers and two drivers overturned on Hungary's M3 motorway near Mezokeresztes at about 01:00 local time on August 16, killing 12 people. Emergency services later reported 47 injured, including 10 seriously. Police detained the driver.

key.title: Landslide hits apartment in Geoje, South Korea, killing one

records.note: 04:42 KST August 17 is August 16 UTC. SBS initially gave approximately 04:30; both times yield the same UTC date. Four injuries were regional, not all at this apartment. Remove unsupported rainfall superlative.

changes.description: A rain-triggered landslide struck a ground-floor apartment in Okpo-dong, Geoje, early on August 17 local time. Three people were rescued; one subsequently died. The other two survived.

key.title: Russian drone strike on Dniprovska mine near Pavlohrad kills one worker

records.note: Reports identify the DTEK mine and one dead/one injured. Concise replacement avoids attributing the mine identification solely to the regional governor.

changes.description: Russian drones struck the Dniprovska mine in the Bohdanivske community of Dnipropetrovsk region on August 17, killing one employee and injuring another, according to DTEK and local reporting.

key.title: Ukrainian missile strikes on Koloskovo in Belgorod region kill six

records.note: The August 17 morning announcement supports six reported deaths and four injuries but does not establish whether the strike was before or after midnight UTC. Border distance is 15 miles, about 24 km, not 15 km. Short proposed prose removes the unsupported distance and burning detail; date remains unresolved.

changes.description: Russian regional authorities reported that a Ukrainian missile attack on Koloskovo in Belgorod region killed six people and injured four, including a child. The announcement was made on August 17; the precise UTC date of the attack remains unestablished.

key.title: Russian missile strike on Pechenihy in Kharkiv region kills ten

records.note: Morning August 18 strike and ten deaths supported. Injuries rose from early 8/17 to 18, then over 20 in local reporting; avoid freezing a superseded number. Political context is unnecessary to the incident.

changes.description: A Russian missile strike hit the centre of Pechenihy in Kharkiv region on the morning of August 18, killing ten people, Ukrainian officials said. Shops, a post office and residential buildings were damaged, and numerous people were injured.

key.title: Pickup-truck collision on Gwalior-Bhind highway kills eight labourers

records.note: PTI places the crash around 01:00 IST August 18, or August 17 UTC. Injury reports vary between 23 and 32; replacement retains only the agreed death toll and avoids a false precise injury total.

changes.description: A pickup carrying migrant labourers collided with a dumper truck near Chhimka in Bhind district around 01:00 local time on August 18. Eight people were killed and numerous others injured.

key.title: School shooting in Zamboanga City kills one and injures nine

records.note: Two deaths include the attacker. GMA places gunfire at approximately 07:45 PHT August 18, or August 17 UTC, not 08:30. Reports conflict on grade level (7/8/9); omit it and unestablished rifle detail.

changes.title: School shooting in Zamboanga City leaves two dead, including attacker
changes.description: A student shot another student and then himself at Ateneo de Zamboanga University's junior high school campus in Zamboanga City on the morning of August 18 local time. Police and the university confirmed two deaths, including the attacker.

key.title: Gold mine collapse on Cameroon-CAR border kills over 100 miners

records.note: CAR authorities locate the mine in their territory; some initial Cameroonian reports mislocate it. The 107 figure is the Garoua-Boulai mayor's provisional recovery account, not a final CAR-confirmed count. CAR prosecutors said the exact total was still being determined. Retain that contradiction explicitly; final toll is unresolved.

changes.description: An artisanal gold mine collapsed at Zamboye near the Cameroon border on August 18. Local reporting attributed 107 recovered bodies to Garoua-Boulai's mayor; AP reported more than 100 deaths, while CAR authorities said the exact toll was still being established.

key.title: Israeli airstrike on cafe near Gaza Port kills six

records.note: Incident and six deaths corroborated. Remove unsupported deadliest-in-weeks claim and unrelated diplomatic assertions.

changes.description: An Israeli strike hit a crowded seaside cafe near Gaza City's fishing port on August 18, killing six Palestinians, including a child, according to medical and eyewitness reports.

key.title: Torrential rains in southwest China kill ten

records.note: August 19 is publication date. Ten combines five in a Guangxi construction-site landslide on Monday August 17 and five in a Changning, Sichuan banquet-wall collapse at 17:30 CST August 18. This is not one August 19 incident.
